name: Iapetus
tagline: Saturn's two-faced moon — one hemisphere bright as snow, the other dark as coal.
history: Iapetus presents the most extreme two-tone face in the Solar System: the leading hemisphere is coated in dark material (probably migrated from outer moon Phoebe) while the trailing side gleams white. A bizarre 20-km-high equatorial ridge — the 'walnut ridge' — wraps a third of the moon, possibly the remnant of an ancient ring or a frozen-in bulge from faster-spinning days. Its 80° year keeps the strange face slowly turning toward the Sun.
